newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spot up.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spot up.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down on Friday with traders saying demand for funds was decreasing due to fewer new domestic A share issues in the short term.
The annual rate for the most active three-day contract dived to 2.29 percent from 15.62 percent on Thursday.
Turnover fell sharply to 4.53 million lots from 11.26 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"Most institutions which used to be major borrowers during new A share issues did not trade in the past two days," a trader said. "This has caused falls in early-maturing contracts."
Traders expect the rates to regain ground early next week.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly up on speculative buying, traders said.
But market sentiment continued to be weak after prices had fallen for weeks, and the contracts were likely to consolidate in a narrow range next week, they said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose to 122.15 yuan from 121.74 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market expanded to 1.75 million lots from 831,328 lots.
